summary: A much stronger batch than w10: most objects have five recognisable, object-specific premises with real punchlines (calendar that cancelled Monday, notepad's 'call Gran' becoming 'cool gorilla', street sign the town renamed itself after, laminating the Do Not Laminate sign, the shredder that really ate the homework, the projector screen hat). Safety is handled well overall: cigarette, butt and vape are smelly and littery, never glamorous; incense has no religion; the Bible is written as a neutral family book (flagged for the developer's decision). The fixes needed: (1) Legendary names are almost all 'The X That Y' (102 of 112), so naming needs a pass; (2) about 30 Legendaries use the 'for N years / kept for fifty years' formula or are quiet successes; (3) about a dozen Epics are paper avalanches, snowstorms or dominoes; (4) several objects scale one trait across three rarities (greeting card signatures, hole-puncher confetti, receipt-roll length, rubber-band ball, hairpin buns); (5) cross-object copies inside the clusters (greeting card R = pop-up book R, crochet R = knitting R, three bride Legendaries, three lock-picking lines, three floor-spike lines, cigarette L = vape L, cigarette butt = w12 litter). Sensitive fixes: vape flavour appeal, the stained glass's 500-year (church) window, the laser pointer aimed at the sky, the newspaper stack used to light fires, and the paper crane's hospital Legendary. Move mechanics are mostly right, but about 40 poison moves are named as smudges or splashes (poison means stink), about 20 names are garbled repeats, and several Ultimates repeat the Epic name. Replacements and paired names are given for every high and medium item.

patterns.pattern: Legendary name monotony: 102 of 112 Legendaries are 'The X That/Who Y' or 'The X of Y'. This is the batch's main naming problem.
patterns.suggestion: Per-object names are given wherever the Legendary lore changes (about 70). For the kept lines, cut 'The X That...' down to at most a fifth of the batch: use 'Name, the Epithet', 'Name the Adjective', pun names and titles, as the replacements show.

patterns.pattern: Paper-spill Epics: about a dozen Epics are 'everything fell / avalanche / snowstorm / blizzard / domino / ankle-deep paper'.
patterns.suggestion: Keep at most four (file folder cabinet, folder on the bus, bookshelf dominoes, calendar page office snow) and change the rest (replacements given).

patterns.pattern: Legendary formula 'has done X for N years / kept for fifty years / never once / still there': about 30 Legendaries.
patterns.suggestion: Replace each with an outrageous feat and a punchline (replacements given).

patterns.pattern: One trait scaled across three rarities: greeting card (signed by everyone U/E/L), hole puncher (confetti C/E/L), receipt roll (long receipt C/E/L), rubber band (ball R/E/L), hairpin (buns U/E/L), plus two-rarity repeats in calendar page, atlas, magazine stack, flyer, ticket, tie clip, thimble small, picture book, paper clip, stained glass.
patterns.suggestion: Five premises per object; replacements are given for the repeated rarities.

patterns.pattern: Cross-object near-copies: greeting card R = pop-up book R (paper castle that won't fold back); crochet hook R = knitting needles R (scarf on one bus ride); hula hoop E = trading card E (craze through every school in town); hair clip E = hair tie E (every ponytail); three bride Legendaries (hair clip, safety pin, pin cushion); three lock-picking lines (hairpin R, paper clip R, credit card L); three floor-spike lines (hairpin C, push pin U, thumbtack C); brochure C = leaflet C; newspaper C = newspaper stack U; file folder R = folder R; cigarette L = vape L; cigarette butt C and L = w12 x_litter U and L; easel E = w12 i_tripod E; comic E = w08 x_bento_box E.
patterns.suggestion: The issue on each object says which side to change; keep the side that is more specific to its object (pop-up book castle, knitting bus scarf, paper clip lock).

patterns.pattern: Cluster tell-apart. Notebooks: diary = lock and secrets; journal = explorer notes; notebook pad = school notes; notepad = phone messages; planner = schedules. Folders: file folder = filing cabinet; folder = school bag; ring binder = rings and dividers. Cards: birthday card = tune and money; greeting card = messages and size. Frames: photo frame = the photo's mood; picture frame = making things look valuable; wall art = abstract; painting = following eyes. Thimbles: thimble = tapping and pushing; small thimble = tiny uses. Pins: push pin = notices; thumbtack = scattering tin; safety pin = rescues; pin cushion = hedgehog look.
patterns.suggestion: The per-object replacements follow this split.

patterns.pattern: Poison moves named as smudges, splodges or splashes (about 40, mostly kit.ink_splatter). Under the house rules poison means stink.
patterns.suggestion: Add a smell word (pong, whiff, stale, musty, rusty, fumes): replacements are given per move.

patterns.pattern: Garbled repeated move names: four or five copies of one word ('Fold Fold Fold Fold Fold', 'Page Page Page Page Page', 'Pin Pin Pin Pin Pin', 'Clip Clip Clip Clip Clip'), or a doubled word on single-hit moves ('Thread Thread Thread', 'Story Boost Boost', 'Snap Startle Snap'), plus de-duplication suffixes ('Muse Boost Art', 'Desk Rest Ruler', 'Wrist Rest Band').
patterns.suggestion: At most three copies, only on ×3 moves; replacements given.

patterns.pattern: Sensitive objects. Cigarette and butt: no glamour, smoke shown as smell and litter (good); the Legendaries model quitting and beach cleaning, but they copy each other and w12. Vape: the Uncommon and Rare name advertise strawberry flavour (fix). Incense: no religion (good). Bible: neutral family book (good); developer decision flagged. Stained glass: the Legendary's 500 years implies a church (fix). Also: the laser-pointer Rare aims at the sky, the newspaper-stack Rare lights fires, three lines teach lock-picking, and the paper-crane Legendary is set around a child in hospital.
patterns.suggestion: Replacements are given; none adds glamour, religion or unsafe how-to.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates that repeat the Epic name ('Card Avalanche', 'Card House Collapse', 'Message Mix-Up Stink', 'Yellow Out', 'Order Chaos', 'Paper Storm', 'Wall Takeover') or promise one effect when variants differ ('Hot Hair Clamp', 'Receipt Pile Daze', 'Shiny Clip Glare', 'Chalk Dust Cloud', 'Beach Litter Pong', 'Hot Tip Spark', 'Staple Snatch'); fixed-burn moves with no heat ('Crane Swarm Flight', 'Torch Under Duvet', 'Snap Sting', 'Bedtime Glow').
patterns.suggestion: Give each Ultimate its own effect-neutral image; add a heat word to every burn move.

patterns.pattern: Many Commons and Uncommons are under 60 characters (about 90 lines, e.g. 'Stabs olives at every party.', 'Sits on your finger like a tiny hat.'). Most are fine habits; the shortest need a small consequence.
